title: [Devlog]: Buses, skyscrapers, elevators for procedurally generated city
author: AlbinoGrimby
selftext:
I posted about this game engine I built with Claude Code about 3 months ago and a lot has changed since then! I've built a procedurally generated city with Claude's help. All of the roads, buildings, terrain, clouds are built using some form of generation. All of this is running relatime on my Linux box (Vulkan), but it also works on mac (Metal), Windows, and webGPU (although probably not this massive city). 

If you watch the video you'll see it stutter a bit as I move around since I've been adding some new experimental features and that's causing framerate hitches. 

Over the past week I've added interiors to buildings so most of the buildings you see are now enter-able. Skyscrapers have lobbies and from there you can take an elevator up or the stairs to access the upper floors. Buildings also have fake windows from the outside (a la the cube map projection trick Insomiac did in Spiderman). The fake views into the buildings do not match the real empty floors of the interior, but it gives a skyscraper some more visual interest from the outside.

Buses are something new I added over the last couple of days. There are procedurally generated bus routes that run throughout the city. The simple UI will tell you when you're near a bus stop and when the bus is arriving. You can enter a bus and move around freely, find a seat, and enjoy the ride. 

The AI also made improvements to the traffic. All of the cars are driven by "agents" (in the video game-y/simulation sense of the word). So they see where they are going and brake and go as needed. Why the vehicles swerve left to right randomly I am not sure of yet -- a future bug to fix. There are also more NPCs and city simulation which is causing the frame rate issues. 

There's still some (hilarious) bugs.

Also, in this video I spawn a car and go on a joyride, and it ends badly for who I thought was 1 NPC standing in the middle of the road.
